newsitem.title: UK: Options-Small coffee skew seen before frost season.
newsitem.headline: Options-Small coffee skew seen before frost season.

text.p: Implied volatilities in nearby LIFFE coffee options were slightly inverted, favouring July, before Brazil's frost season starts in June, traders said on Thursday.

Traders pegged at-the-money implied volatility at 38.5 percent, slightly higher than the next month September's 38.0 percent and up from Wednesday's 37.5 percent. November volatility stood near 41 percent.
July was marked higher due to risks that signs of frost may emerge in Brazil, traders said. The last major frosts in 1994 damaged many Brazilian coffee trees and sparked a worldwide price surge.

But that inversion has remained small because locals have been discounting chances of a frost. Surprisingly, a trader said selling interest emerged in July near 40 percent volatility, which was already seen as historically low.

September and November saw hints of buying interest in $1,700 and $1,750 options but traders said locals have not yet been ready to offer the options. November options have only been offered with a very wide bid/ask spread of 40/60 because of frost risks, they said.

Though July volatilities were historically low and the skew has remained small, one trader said he expected the skew to widen as cold weather moves into Brazil. If Brazil gets cold, he said volatilities could easily jump 10 percent.

If coffee futures extend their recent rally and break out of its trading range since about early March, volatility could also spike higher. The trader was eyeing a breakout above $1,700 to initially prod volatilities higher.
This morning, 200 July $1750/$1900 call spreads changed hands, traders said. The July calls traded at a 1.5-percent discount to the calls, which traders said was in-line with the settlement skew.
Overall activity this week has been scattered from various clients, with little fund hedging seen.
In cocoa, prices were being quoted, but very few options actually traded. At-the-money implied volatilities were seen near steady, with July's midpoint near 31 percent.
